items.title: Anonymous POST create item is 401
items.reason: Core of the bug: anonymous create returned 201, letting anyone add products. Functional layer because it needs the real API pipeline and auth middleware.

items.title: Anonymous PUT v2 update item is 401
items.reason: Anonymous update changed prices and published a price event. Separate case from create because it is a different endpoint registration (`UpdateItem`).

items.title: Anonymous PUT v1 update item is 401
covers: Technical Notes: UpdateItemV1 mapped without RequireAuthorization
items.reason: The v1 update is a separate route (`UpdateItemV1`) that could be missed when securing v2; a gap would leave a bypass.

items.title: Anonymous DELETE item is 401
items.reason: Anonymous delete returned 204, so anyone could remove products. Separate endpoint registration (`DeleteItemById`).

items.title: Rejected anonymous writes leave the catalog unchanged
covers: Actual: anyone can change products and prices
items.reason: Guards against auth that runs after the handler (status 401 but data still changed, price event still published). Checks persisted state across all three write verbs together.

items.title: Invalid bearer token on write is 401
items.reason: Proves the JWT bearer validation is actually wired in Catalog.API, not just a presence check on the header.

items.title: Authenticated non-admin user gets 403 on write
covers: Expected: only an admin role can change the catalog
items.reason: Authentication alone must not be enough; the policy requires role `Admin`. Without this case a fix that only requires any valid token would pass.

items.title: Admin can create an item
covers: Expected: only an admin role can change the catalog
items.reason: Ensures the fix did not lock out legitimate admins; creation is the first of the three writes.

items.title: Admin can update an item and the change persists
covers: Expected: only an admin role can change the catalog
items.reason: Update is the write that publishes the price-changed event, so the admin path must still work end to end.

items.title: Admin can delete an item
covers: Expected: only an admin role can change the catalog
items.reason: Ensures the delete endpoint still works for admins after authorization was added.

items.title: Catalog reads stay anonymous
items.reason: The WebApp and Basket/Ordering read the catalog without a token; a global requirement would break the storefront.

covers: Acceptance Criteria: test.fixme removed and the rest of the file still passes
